newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH BUDGET NEEDS PREVENT TAX CUT IN 1997 - PM.
newsitem.headline: POLISH BUDGET NEEDS PREVENT TAX CUT IN 1997 - PM.

text.p: Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said on Tuesday that a constitutional court ruling granting pensioners overdue benefit rises makes an earlier planned cut in 1997 income tax unlikely.
"The government proposals to meet earlier obligations and lower taxes has been put forward in different circumstances," Cimoszewicz told reporters before a cabinet meeting.
"A constitutional tribunal ruling regarding cost-of-living increases of pensions and disability benefits...and its implementation means new budget expenditures," he said.
The constitutional court ruled in July that the government owed pensioners up to 8.3 billion zlotys in benefit increases it should have granted them last March.
The government decided after the ruling it would not amend its 1996 budget and the need of extra payout should be taken into account in next year's budget.

Coalition deputies from three parliamentary commissions decided last week to recommend that the full parliment maintained personal income taxes at this year's level rather than cut them as proposed in the 1997 budget outline.
Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko said on Monday a possible decision to keep taxes unchanged would be a mistake.
"If taxes are not cut in line with government proposals it will be a bad decision," Gazeta Wyborcza quoted Kolodko as saying.
Under the original plan 1997's personal income tax levels were to be lowered to 20, 31 i 43 percent from the present 21, 33 and 45 percent respectively.
The Sejm, lower house, is due to vote on income tax bills in the second half of October.
